questions.skill: Generate several same-size random samples with random digits and see how the estimates vary
questions.prompt: A school has 100 students numbered 00 to 99. Students 00 to 39 chose art as their favorite class. Use these random two-digit numbers to choose a sample of 5 students: 07  52  31  88  14 What percent of the sample chose art?
questions.prompt_markup:
A school has 100 students numbered 00 to 99. Students 00 to 39 chose art as their favorite class.
Use these random two-digit numbers to choose a sample of 5 students:
07  52  31  88  14
What percent of the sample chose art?

questions.skill: Generate several same-size random samples with random digits and see how the estimates vary
questions.prompt: Students 00 to 39 of a school of 100 chose art. Four random samples of 5 students were chosen with random digits: Sample 1: 07 52 31 88 14 Sample 2: 45 63 02 97 71 Sample 3: 38 19 60 25 84 Sample 4: 50 11 76 93 66 What is the range of the four sample percents?
questions.prompt_markup:
Students 00 to 39 of a school of 100 chose art. Four random samples of 5 students were chosen with random digits:
Sample 1: 07 52 31 88 14
Sample 2: 45 63 02 97 71
Sample 3: 38 19 60 25 84
Sample 4: 50 11 76 93 66
What is the range of the four sample percents?

questions.skill: Generate several same-size random samples with random digits and see how the estimates vary
questions.prompt: Students 00 to 39 of a school of 100 chose art, so the true percent is 40%. Four random samples of 5 students gave 60%, 20%, 60%, and 20%. What is the mean of the four sample percents? How does it compare with the true percent, and how much do single samples vary?
questions.prompt_markup:
Students 00 to 39 of a school of 100 chose art, so the true percent is 40%. Four random samples of 5 students gave 60%, 20%, 60%, and 20%.
What is the mean of the four sample percents? How does it compare with the true percent, and how much do single samples vary?
questions.correct_answer: The mean is 40%, the same as the true percent, but single samples varied from 20% to 60%.
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the mean 40%, and the variation of single samples.

sections.skill: Use the spread of simulated samples to give an interval for a population percent

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use the spread of simulated samples to give an interval for a population percent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Simulations show that the middle 95% of random samples of 50 students land within 10 percentage points of the true percent. A real random sample of 50 gives 44%. What interval is likely to contain the population percent?
questions.prompt_markup:
